      <description>Den britiske komikeren og skuespilleren David Walliams anklages av ei rekke kvinner for å ha brukt kjendisstatusen sin for å tilnærme seg unge kvinner seksuelt.

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/norge-gir-600-regnskogmillioner-til-brasil-1.18077109</link>
      <description>Klimaminister Sigrun Aasland (Ap) har med en stor sum når hun mandag reiser til åpningen av klimatoppmøtet i Tyrkia.
– Vi har med 600 millioner kroner til Brasil, for de har levert veldig gode resultater på å hindre avskoging i 2025, sier Aasland.
Brasil har det siste året redusert avskogningen til det laveste nivået siden målingene staret for over 40 år siden.
Gjennom den norske regnskogsatsingen gir Norge økonomisk støtte til Brasil når de klarer å redusere avskogingen.

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/kongen-fullforte-maraton-pa-tiden-4.43.01-1.18076803</link>
      <description>Kongen og kronprinsessen er deltakere i French Riviera Marathon, i Nice sør i Frankrike.
Kong Haakon løp i mål på tiden 4.43.01, ifølge sporingstjenesten Trackanza.
Det var TV 2 som meldte saken først.
Et bilde viser kongen og kronprinsessen løpende ved siden av hverandre under maratonet. I maratonet er kronprinsessen registrert som Ingrid Alexandra og kongen som Haakon Magnus.
Startskuddet gikk klokka 09.16, og distansen er helmaraton på 42,125 kilometer. Løypen går langs den franske rivieraen fra Nice til Cannes.
Lørdag formiddag opplyste Slottet på nettsidene sine at «statsrådet forestår bestyrelsen av riket».
Ifølge nettsidene var kongen og kronprinsessen på privat opphold i utlandet. Det betyr at regjeringen har ansvaret for å styre og forvalte landet.
(NTB/NRK)</description>

    <item>
      <title>Ny norsk gulltriumf i VM i skyting</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/ny-norsk-gulltriumf-i-vm-i-skyting-1.18076796</link>
      <description>Caroline Finnestad Lund, Jeanette Hegg Duestad og Synnøve Berg tok laggullet på 50 meter rifle match i VM i skyting i Doha søndag.
Det var Lunds andre gull i mesterskapet. Lørdag ble 21-åringen verdensmester på 50 meter 60 skudd liggende.
Norge sanket totalt 1764 poeng under lagkonkurransen, og de kom 3,0 poeng foran Sveits på 2.-plass. Tsjekkia stakk av med bronsemedaljen. De var to poeng bak sveitserne igjen.
I eliminasjonen for lag 1 ble Finnestad Lund nummer fire med 588 poeng. Synnøve Berg ble nummer sju med 586 poeng. Duestad ble nummer tre med 590 poeng i lag 2.
Alle de tre norske jentene er videre til kvalifiseringen i den individuelle konkurransen i den samme øvelsen mandag. (NTB)</description>

      <title>Flere skadet etter kraftig jordskjelv sentralt i Japan</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/flere-skadet-etter-kraftig-jordskjelv-sentralt-i-japan-1.18076688</link>
      <description>Minst 22 personer ble skadet da et jordskjelv med styrke 5,5 rammet Shizuoka-prefekturet i det sentrale Japan. Butikkvinduer ble knust, og folk rømte ut av bygninger.
Ifølge kringkasteren NHK er det ikke fare for tsunamier.
Skjelvet inntraff rundt klokka 1 natt til søndag. Det hadde en dybde på 41 kilometer. Den foreløpige målingen fra Japans meteorologiske institutt, som har ansvaret for overvåking og varsling av jordskjelv, var på 5,7.
Det amerikanske jordskjelvsenteret USGS målte det til 5,5.
I naboprefekturet Aichi ble det målt kraftige rystelser på nivå 5+ på den japanske skalaen – det sterkeste som er registrert der siden 1997.
(NTB)</description>

      <description>Israels president har gitt opposisjonsleder Gadi Eisenkot i oppdrag å prøve danne regjering.
Hverken partiene som støtter statsminister Benjamin Netanyahu eller partiene som støtter Eisenkot fikk flertall ved valget 27. november.
Netanyahus blokk fikk 53 plasser i Knesset, mens blokken til Eisenkot fikk 48 mandater.
For å få flertall og bli statsminister trenger man 61 plasser i nasjonalforsamlingen. Begge blokkene er avhengig av de 19 mandatene fra de palestinsk-arabiske partiene, mend både Netanyahu og Eisenkot har sagt de ikke vil forhandle med dem.</description>

      <description>Casper Ruud har storspilt i Paris denne uken. Nå er han klar for semifinale etter seier over Nuno Borges.
Ruuds oppgjør mot portugiseren endte med 7-6 (7-5), 6-4. De to møttes for bare ni dager siden i Basel, og da snudde Borges kampen til seier.
Ruud og Borges kom til semifinalen proppfulle av selvtillit: Ingen har tapt ett sett på veien, og de hadde heller ikke gitt fra seg mer enn fire game i noen av settene.
Ruud spilte kvartfinale i Paris Masters for andre gang. For Borges, som står med én tittel i karrieren (ATP250), var dette første kvartfinale på Masters- eller Grand Slam-nivå.</description>

      <description>Politiet opplyser at det har vært en front-mot-front-ulykke på E6 like ved Eidsvoll-tunnelen i sørgående løp.

Det satt en person i hver av bilene. En av dem er bekreftet død, den andre er kritisk skadet.

      <description>Thomas Markle ble pågrepet av føderale agenter i nærheten av Tampa i Florida fredag morgen amerikansk tid.

      <title>NFF innfører semiautomatisert offside i Eliteserien</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/nff-innforer-semiautomatisert-offside-i-eliteserien-1.18075445</link>
      <description>Det opplyser Fotballforbundet på en pressekonferanse fredag.
– Prisen har kommet ned til et nivå som gjør at muligheten er der, sier generalsekretær Karl-Petter Løken.
Han opplyser at innføringen vil skje i tråd med et dommerløft. NFF bevilger 5,5 millioner kroner i 2027 til dommerløftet, og 3,5 millioner av dem skal få til semiautomatisert offside.
NFF ønsker å øke dette til 7,5 millioner kroner i 2028, og gradvis trappe opp mot 2030.
– Det du har sett med disse linjene blir borte og du får disse visningene med menneskekropper hvor du ser helt tydelig at det er offside. Det er semiautomatisert offside. Det er det ene løftet, sier Løken og fortsetter:
– Det er en utgift som tas én gang og som vil følge oss, og så vil vi trappe opp resten av investeringen i dommerutviklingene i de andre tiltakene i tillegg. Så det blir en gradvis opptrapping, eksempelvis profesjonalisering. Vi starter stille og rolig og så blir det flere og flere.
Dette skjer etter et VAR-oppgjør blant flere toppklubber. Roenborg satt ned et eget utvalg som konkluderte med at «Dagens VAR fungerer for dårlig under norske forhold. De lovte forbedringene har ikke løst hovedutfordringene, og kostnadene er for høye i forhold til kvaliteten».
Utvalget til Rosenborg stilte seg også tvilende til at semiautomatisert offside ville hjelpe VAR i norsk fotball.
– Så det vil være penger ut av vinduet hvis tinget sier nei (til VAR)? spør NRK.
– Vi kommer ikke til å diskutere detaljer i den avtalen, svarer Klaveness.</description>

CHEK https://cheknews.ca/ Independent and employee owned - local news stories, weather, sports, events and more Wed, 11 Nov 2026 02:39:37 +0000 en-CA hourly 1 https://cheknews.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/cropped-CHEK-Mark-512x512-1-200x200.png?crop=1 CHEK https://cheknews.ca/ 32 32 70014466 Nanaimo bakery goes cashless after two recent break-ins and thefts https://cheknews.ca/nanaimo-bakery-goes-cashless-after-two-recent-break-ins-and-thefts-1360565/ Wed, 11 Nov 2026 01:22:23 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1360565

A Nanaimo Cafe and Bakery is going cashless after two recent break-ins and thefts.

The post Nanaimo bakery goes cashless after two recent break-ins and thefts appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

A Nanaimo Cafe and Bakery is going cashless after two recent break-ins and thefts.

The owner says the thefts represent a significant loss and so he’s had to make the difficult decision to remove cash to hopefully deter anyone from breaking into his bakery again.

The Misty Pines Cafe & Bakery in Nanaimo’s Old City Quarter has new signs by its front door and on its till, telling customers it’s no longer accepting cash.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

“I think it’s a real shame and it’s happening so often and I think it’s a shame that businesses have to resort to that measure,” said Tammy Bennett, a customer.

The first break-in happened Sept. 6 when two thieves gained access to the building and stole the safe and cash float. Just over a month later on Oct. 10, a thief broke in again. The second time, the thief time to wrench the safe from the wall and stole what was now a different, larger safe. He took it and the cash float again. This time, with cameras in a different location, the video images are better and the bakery’s owner says he recognized him.

“As soon as I saw him the second time on the camera because same outfit and same person looking like the same person as the first one,” said John Akin, owner of the Misty Pines Cafe & Bakery.

Based on the video surveillance, police arrested a suspect later that same day; it turns out he was wanted on an outstanding warrant. After spending hours in jail, he was released the next morning on a promise to appear in court.

“It is upsetting. It’s hard to be a small business,” said Akin. “I think the main problem is the justice system currently in Canada.”

Akin says the bakery had roughly $6,000 stolen in the two break-ins, an amount he calls significant.

Even though 10 per cent of the bakery’s purchases are in cash, he says it makes the most sense to no longer use it.

“Sometimes people miscalculate, like all the time I see shortages on the cash, cash outs like it brings more trouble,” said Akin.

Alberto Castillo was supporting the bakery today after his wife saw the social media post about the thefts and the decision to go cashless.

“It sucks. Obviously, everything is going digital now and now usually everyone has their stuff on their phone, but I still prefer cash sometimes,” said Castillo.

The suspect, who can’t be named, as he hasn’t been formally charged yet, is facing charges of break and enter, theft under $5,000 and possession of stolen property related to the second theft at the bakery, with a first court date set for Dec. 15.

Last year a business owner in the same area as the bakery decided to no longer keep cash in her store overnight after a break-in and theft.

The post Nanaimo bakery goes cashless after two recent break-ins and thefts appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

There’s new ownership stirring the pot at one of B.C.’s most beloved tea shops, but don’t expect the recipe to change.

Murchie’s Fine Tea & Coffee, a fixture for tea lovers for 132 years, has a new owner. As of Nov. 1, all eight locations were purchased by B.C.-based Dig Collective, a family-run company led by president Aaron Saks.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

And while the new owners might not fit the stereotypical image of a tea shop proprietor, they say they know better than to mess with a good thing.

“We have no intention of making any major changes,” Saks said.

That’s welcome news for the loyal customers who treat Murchie’s as more than just a place to pick up their favourite blend.

Take Dianne Whyte, for example. When asked if she lives at Murchie’s, her answer was simple: “I live at Murchie’s. I have a table in the back.”

She hasn’t met the new owners yet, but she’s already giving them the thumbs-up.

The acquisition adds a fifth brand to Dig Collective’s portfolio, joining West Coast Seeds, Renee’s Garden, Urban Bee Supplies and Pinebush Home and Garden.

As Saks puts it: “Birds, bees, seeds, and now teas.”

The company may be new to the tea business, but the family behind it is no stranger to B.C. business. The Diamond family has operated Delta-based organic seed company West Coast Seeds since 1983. Its patriarch, the late Jack Diamond, was a businessman and philanthropist whose first business venture dates back to 1940.

Saks says he quickly learned just how seriously Murchie’s history is taken. During his first conversation with building owner Bob Louie, one message came through loud and clear.

“He just kept reiterating, ‘You cannot screw this up, this is a heritage business’” Saks recalled.

For now, customers can expect the familiar sights, smells and flavours that have made Murchie’s a Government Street institution, including the tea-drinking mechanical grannies at the front of the shop and the treats being made downstairs.

Assistant pastry chef Stefan Ouellette suggests pairing a cup of tea with a fruit tart or crème brûlée. And don’t overlook the shortbread, either.

There’s a Scottish connection there, too. Murchie’s founder John Murchie was born in Scotland and famously delivered tea to Queen Victoria at Balmoral Castle.

More than a century later, the shop is still steeped in that heritage.

The owners may be new, but the message is familiar: quality comes first, tradition matters, and there’s always time for tea.

After all, 132 years is a pretty good steep.

The post Visibility key for being seen on B.C. roads this fall appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Fog and poor road conditions didn’t stop one truck driver from travelling well above the speed limit, with the incident caught on camera by a BC Highway Patrol officer.

While police issued about 1,200 fewer tickets during this year’s “Drive Relative to Conditions Month” campaign compared to last year, Sgt. Michael McLaughlin, media relations officer with BC Highway Patrol, said too many drivers are still failing to slow down when weather conditions deteriorate.

Watch the video below:

Loading the player...

“We’re not in summer weather. You are way more likely to get into a serious collision that you can’t avoid if you are speeding in these terrible weather conditions,” McLaughlin said.

With morning commutes now taking place in darkness and often accompanied by rain, drivers need to be especially cautious behind the wheel, according to Kate Harris, CEO of Drivewise Driving School.

“People are tired when they are waking up. And when you are driving to and from work, and you’re tired, it’s dark, and rainy, and visibility is not good. That’s a trifecta of something that could happen on the roads,” Harris said.

Colleen Woodger, regional road safety co-ordinator, ICBC said at this time of year it’s critical to be vigilant.

“The most dangerous time, actually, for pedestrian collisions is during these fall and winter months. We do see a spike in October and November in pedestrian collisions. About 42 per cent of all of our pedestrian collisions happen in these months,” Woodger said.

“It’s darker longer in the morning. It’s going to cover your entire morning commute. Darkness is a factor when it comes to these collisions,” McLaughlin said. ” Safety-wise, you have to be a lot more careful with traffic, bikes and pedestrians. Even at the best of times, when it’s darker and rainy, you have to be careful.”

With daylight hours dwindling and wet roads becoming the norm, taking extra precautions behind the wheel could mean the difference between life and death.

“Birding has been a passion of mine every since I was the height of a heron,” said Newell.

“Birding is like going on a treasure hunt, you just never know what you’re going to see.”

When Newell spotted one brown, amidst a sea of black and blue last Wednesday, initially he didn’t know what to do.

“I knew exactly what I’d seen right away but there’s always that moment of, ‘Is this actually happening?'” said Newell. “I had to pinch myself to make sure it’s real because it’s a bird I’ve been dreaming of seeing in Victoria for a long time.”

Gliding among a flock of surf scoters off the shores of Saanich’s Glencoe Cove-Kwatsech Park, Newell had spotted a Steller’s Eider.

“It was a dream come true, that’s the best way I can put it. It was dream come true,” said Newell.

The arctic duck is a once-in-a-lifetime species that rarely makes it past the 60th parallel.

“The last time one was here was 50 years ago,” said Ann Nightingale, a fellow bird enthusiast and volunteer with Rocky Point Bird Observatory.

For many B.C. birders, it’s the holy grail. And it’s drawing “twitchers” from near and far.

“The word got out in an instant. There was probably 60 people here later that day,” said Nightingale.

“There have been lots of cars and lots of people,” said Joan Mcneely, who lives in the neigbourhood. “They were all very excited.”

The Steller’s Eider seeking shelter off Saanich’s shores is female. She’s cinnamon brown, and much more sensible looking than her male counterpart in the high arctic with his mix of pure white and orange plumage, black circle surrounding its eye, and iridescent moss-green smudge on its hindcrown.

But given their shrinking species, it’s a thrilling find.

“They’ve gone through significant declines, so the North American population is just a few thousand,” said Newell.

Newell and Nightingale surmise the lone ranger is here on vacation, enjoying the Salish Sea’s shellfish platter for the season before it migrates back to the high arctic to mate.

“If the bird was to over-winter, I wouldn’t be surprised,” said Newell. “And as long as the bird is still being seen, I think more and more people will come for it.”

The Gulf Islands National Park Reserve will no longer have a dedicated park warden detachment after cuts to Parks Canada.

Budget cuts recently mean that 13 park warden detachments across the country will be closing, among them is the Gulf Islands detachment.

“On Vancouver Island, the Gulf Islands detachment will be closing, but the Pacific Rim detachment is gaining one permanent position, for a total of 5 permanent, year-round park wardens,” a Parks Canada spokesperson said in an email. “Gulf Islands will be served by the park wardens in Pacific Rim.”

The Gulf Islands National Park Reserve covers 15 islands and 30 islets.

Parks Canada argues that regionalizing park law enforcement will “strengthen officer safety by improving access to backup support when needed and increase our ability to deploy resources effectively across a broader area.”

However, Athena George, who is a former park interpreter for the Gulf Islands National Park Reserve, says this is a loss for the community.

“The patrols that are here and have been year-round in Gulf Islands would go out in their boat. They knew the islands intimately,” George said on a Zoom interview.

“They know the zones, there’s certain zones in the park that are highly protected for ecological integrity and for cultural sensitivity, they knew these places. They checked them to make sure nobody was in them, messing around there. They knew the spots to look for illegal camping.”

Now, with the Gulf Islands National Park Reserve having park wardens operating out of Pacific Rim, she’s wondering about the logistics.

“I’m dumbfounded,” she said. “Do they know that Gulf Islands National Parkers is 300 kilometres away from Pacific Rim National Park Reserve? So I’m not sure how that works.”

Similarly, Elizabeth May, Green Party of Canada leader and MP for Saanich—Gulf Islands, is wondering how the decision was made.

“Someone in Ottawa hasn’t looked at a map,” May said. “I mean, these are not adjacent areas at all.”

May says she’s calling the cuts to Parks Canada a double whammy.

“Whammy one is oh yes, it’s wonderful. We want Canadians to go visit the parks, so we have the Canada Strong Pass, which is great that Canadians can go to the national parks for free,” May said in a Zoom interview.

“Great, but what it’s meant is there’s additional stress on the staff, the interpreters, on keeping the campsites clean, making sure everything is looked after, safety concerns, fire hazard, whatever other events could be going on within national parks, and encounters with dangerous wildlife. All of those require real people on the ground.”

May says when Parliament is back in session, she’ll be pushing for answers about how this will work.

“You can’t possibly have the Gulf Islands National Park Reserve with one warden in Pacific Rim,” she said.

“If it wasn’t that it made me so angry, I’d laugh because this is a joke. It’s not funny, but just look at a map.”

George has launched a petition calling for the government to stop cuts to Parks Canada, and hopes that people will write to government voicing their opposition.

“I really would like people, if you care about your national parks, to write to Julie Dabrusin. She is the minister of environment, climate change and nature for Canada,” George said.

“So let her know that you care about your parks, and you don’t want the cuts to happen.”

The University of Victoria’s women’s rugby team won their first-ever national championship this weekend in a blowout game against the University of British Columbia.

After three straight years of finishing runner-up, the Vikes beat the defending champion, UBC, in a 17-0 game at the U Sports Canada final on Sunday in Guelph, Ontario.

UVic’s Emily Findlay, Piper Walsh and Larah Wright scored the tries in the game, ending the Thunderbirds’ bid for a third straight title. 

Findlay was named the Vikes player of the game and was one of four Vikes to be named to the tournament’s all-star team. The others were Walsh, Maggie Mackinnon and Maddy Grant.

Assistant coach Olly Winser says the win was a reflection of how hard the team has worked this year.

“I was surprised at how calm and confident the team felt that morning,” he told CHEK News.

“We’ve been in three other championship finals in the three previous years and didn’t come away with the win, but this year the team felt very confident and calm in the morning. We, the coaching staff, felt like it was a positive sign, and obviously it worked well,” he said.

Winser says beyond any standout moments, the team just seemed to gel this game, with a momentum developing after an early game scrum penalty.

“I think they’re really proud. It’s a team; they all love each other so much and they do an unbelievable amount of work and the culture of the team is really special,” he said. “I think it vindicates all the hard work and sacrifices they put in to be the sacrifices they are.”

Winser also pointed to head coach Brittany Waters for helping develop the team’s defence over the years.

“To shut out a team in a national championship — it’s a testament to her quality, of our team’s defences, and how good a job she’s done coaching that defence,” he said.
